root.claim: There is one deterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes that returns the exact $2n$-bit product of any two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, disproving the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture of Schönhage and Strassen in this model.
root.method: Observe that one machine with a power saving refutes the conjecture; build two tape procedures, a fast interchange of address chunks and a simultaneous butterfly layer, whose recursive costs carry a power saving from linear networks with a rank deficit; then place them inside Harvey and van der Hoeven's reduction of multiplication to synthetic polynomial transforms, accounting for every change of representation, precision and cost.

motivation.text: The transform route already spends $\Theta(n\log n)$ just scanning $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ levels, so beating $n\log n$ needs savings in both data movement and arithmetic, which the two tape procedures supply.

quote.quote: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$. We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic. Two tape procedures supply them;

root.salient: The saving is a strict power of the logarithm, $(\lg n)^{-\kappa}$, holding through all input lengths, so the running time divided by $n\lg n$ tends to zero; the exponent $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is tiny but fixed.

children.claim: Refuting an eventual lower bound $T_A(n)\ge c_An\lg n$ for every machine needs one machine with $\liminf_{n\to\infty}T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$, and a power saving in the logarithm gives limit zero through all input lengths.

quote.quote: Its negation requires one machine satisfying $\liminf_{n\to\infty}T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$. The power saving proved here gives a limit of zero through all input lengths, which is a stronger conclusion.

children.claim: Two fixed-tape procedures run with a power saving: interchanging two disjoint $u$-bit address chunks of an array of volume $V$ costs $O(Vu^\tau)$, and applying the normalized butterfly at one selected bit of each of at most $d$ address chunks of polynomial records costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with fixed $\tau,\lambda'<1$.
children.method: Derive each procedure from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values and restores every scratch value: split array rows cyclically among the $W$ wire roles, give each vertex a frame so that the endpoint effect is the wanted operator and each edge is a few smaller calls of the same procedure, and solve the resulting volume-normalized recurrence.

motivation.text: With rows split among $W$ roles, a call at parameter $mf$ makes $s$ calls at parameter $f$ on streams of volume $V/W$, so per unit volume the cost grows by $s/W$ when the parameter grows by $m$; a network with $s<Wm$ gives an exponent below one.

quote.quote: After dividing cost by volume, multiplying the parameter by $m$ increases the recursive contribution by $s/W<m$. This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

children.salient: Both costs have exponents strictly below one in the parameter, $u^\tau$ and $d^{\lambda'}$, where moving $u$ digits one at a time or applying $D$ butterfly factors separately would cost a full pass per digit or factor.

children.claim: Two fixed linear networks, a bit network over $\mathbb F_2$ with $W_{\rm b}$ wires and a complex network over $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$ with $W_{\rm c}$ wires, each exchange two banks of $N$ values with prescribed signs and restore every scratch wire, and admit frames whose edge changes need $s<Wm$ smaller calls in total, with $m=h^3=10^6$; quantitatively $s/W<m^{1-2^{-50}}$ for both.
children.method: Build the scalar exchange network, show that a frame common to all wires at a gate commutes with the pointwise gate, attach nested subspace labels built from three-element subsets and count their dimension changes, then turn labels into frames: projection-matrix address shears for the bit network and phase operators for the complex network.

motivation.text: A gate acts pointwise, so a representation common to all its wires does not disturb it; the representation may then change along each wire, and subspace labels choose those changes so that each costs few smaller calls.

quote.quote: When the values are replaced by arrays, a common representation on all wires at a gate lets that gate act pointwise without disturbing the representation. We explain this invariant before constructing the subspace labels that make changes of representation cheap.

adds.meaning: The size, 100, of the ground set whose three-element subsets index the data.

children.claim: For arbitrary initial scratch values, the three-stage scalar network sends $(X_a,Y_a)\mapsto(-Y_a,X_a)$ for every index $a$ and restores every scratch wire; in the bit construction this is the permutation exchanging $X_a$ and $Y_a$.
children.method: Run each invocation (one coordinate of the triple index at a time) by the eight-row schedule: subtract side injection and scatter, copy, gather, scatter, side injection, undo gather, undo copy; check that its net effect is $y_S\gets y_S+x_S$ coefficient by coefficient, and compose a forward, an inverse and a forward stage.

motivation.text: Subtracting the effect of the old scratch values before injecting the sources, and undoing copies and gathers afterwards, makes the net change independent of the arbitrary scratch contents and returns them unchanged.

quote.quote: The first two rows of the following schedule remove the effect of the old scratch values; the next four introduce the source values and add their effect to the target; the last two restore the scratch values.

children.salient: The outcome does not depend on the arbitrary initial scratch contents, and every scratch wire ends with its initial value.

children.claim: If the initial side and central vectors are $a,c$, rows 0-1 subtract $\mathcal Ja+\mathcal Rc$ from the target, rows 2-3 change the scratch to $a+\mathcal Vx,c+\mathcal Gx$, rows 4-5 add $\mathcal R(c+\mathcal Gx)+\mathcal J(a+\mathcal Vx)$ and rows 6-7 restore $c,a$, so the net target change is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independent of $a$ and $c$.

quote.quote: The net target change is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independently of $a,c$.

children.claim: In the bit construction the central coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ is $|S\cap T|\bmod2$; side injection cancels exactly the pairs meeting in one point, distinct triples meeting in zero or two points already give zero, and $S=T$ gives one.

quote.quote: In the bit case, the central coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ is $|S\cap T|\bmod2$. The side contribution cancels exactly the intersection-one cases; distinct triples with intersection zero or two already have coefficient zero, and the self coefficient is one.

children.claim: In the complex construction the central coefficient is $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$; side injection cancels it for distinct triples meeting in zero or two points, intersection one contributes zero and $S=T$ gives one, so both nets are $y\gets y+x$.

quote.quote: In the complex case, the central coefficient is $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$. The side cancels it for distinct triples with intersection zero or two; intersection one contributes zero, and the self coefficient is one. Thus both net maps are $y\gets y+x$.

children.claim: A forward stage, an inverse stage ($X\gets X-Y$) and a forward stage take $(x,y)$ to $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$, each invocation restoring its own scratch wires.

quote.quote: Starting from $(x,y)$, the three stages give $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$. Each invocation restores its own auxiliary wires.

children.claim: If every source, gate and sink $v$ carries an invertible frame $D_v$, common to all incidences of a gate, and each edge $u\to v$ applies $D_vD_u^{-1}$, then the array network implements $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$, so a route from input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w$ applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$, scratch roles included.
children.method: Maintain the invariant that the stored array at each vertex is $D_v$ applied to the logical array: define the input's logical interpretation by $D_{\rm in}^{-1}$, let each edge change the frame, and use linearity of the pointwise gates.

motivation.text: Once the scalar routing is fixed, only the endpoint frames determine each route's operator, so the intermediate frames are free to be chosen to make each edge change cheap.

quote.quote: Once the scalar routing is fixed, the endpoint frames determine the array operator on each route; the intermediate frames can then be chosen to make each edge change inexpensive.

children.claim: The physical input $f$ is given the logical interpretation $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$, which needs no tape work, so the invariant holds at the sources.

quote.quote: For a supplied physical input $f$, define its logical interpretation to be $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$; this definition requires no physical preprocessing.

children.claim: An edge changes $D_u\varphi$ into $D_v\varphi$, and at a gate $\sum_jc_jD_v\varphi_j=D_v(\sum_jc_j\varphi_j)$, so the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate and the invariant reaches the sinks.

quote.quote: Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, and the invariant continues to the sinks.

children.claim: For a signed role permutation the route from $w$ to $\rho(w)$ therefore applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$, and every role, auxiliary ones included, enters this identity.

quote.quote: All roles, including the auxiliary roles, enter this identity.

children.claim: Summed over all edges of either network, the absolute changes of label dimension equal $Wm-2N+2L$, where the loss $L=Ich$ on decreasing edges satisfies $L/N=100/539$ (bit) or $101/539$ (complex), below $1/2$; so the total stays below $Wm-N$, leaving a strict deficit $s<Wm$ even after the bit interface adds $N$ source ranks.
children.method: Attach nested nondegenerate subspace labels to every vertex, telescope the signed dimension changes from the terminal labels, confine all decreases to the central-wire returns, and compute the resulting loss exactly.

motivation.text: The terminal labels fix the signed sum of dimension changes at $Wm-2N$, so the absolute sum, which counts the smaller calls, exceeds it only by twice the dimension lost on decreasing edges; keeping that loss small relative to $N$ leaves the saving.

quote.quote: The saving will come from keeping the total dimension lost on decreasing edges small relative to $N$.

children.salient: The deficit is strict but minute: the relative deficits are $\eta_{\rm b}=339/22587335000000$ and $\eta_{\rm c}=73/19906842167500$, about $10^{-11}$, yet any strict deficit $s<Wm$ already makes the recursion exponent smaller than one.

adds.meaning: The total label dimension lost on edges whose label shrinks.

adds.meaning: The number of separate eight-row invocations over the three stages.

children.claim: Nondegenerate subspaces of $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$, of dimension $m=h^3$, can be attached to all sources, gates and sinks so that every edge joins nested labels, the terminal labels run $U_a\to\mathcal F$ on $X_a$, $0\to U_a^\perp$ on $Y_a$ and $0\to\mathcal F$ on scratch wires, and the only decreasing edges are the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4, each losing dimension $h$.

motivation.text: Gather and scatter create coefficients depending on intersection size, and the side wires cancel the unwanted ones; the orthogonality of neighboring indicator vectors is what lets the side-wire labels grow monotonically through the gates.

quote.quote: Orthogonality of the corresponding indicator vectors permits the subspace assignments.

adds.name: ambient label space
adds.meaning: The tensor cube of the triple-indicator space, with its tensor bilinear form, in which all labels lie.

adds.name: triple indicator
adds.meaning: The indicator vector, over the rationals or over the two-element field, of a three-element subset T of the ground set.

quote.quote: Thus every triple line is nondegenerate, and neighboring triple lines are orthogonal, in the label field belonging to either construction.

quote.quote: The ambient label space is $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$ with its tensor bilinear form. It has dimension $m$ and is nondegenerate.

quote.quote: The first inclusion is possible because $t_X\perp t_Y$.

quote.quote: A central wire returns once from the former label to the latter, losing exactly $P\otimes F$. The gate order below confines all decreases to this return, while the other edges realize the prescribed stage transitions.

children.claim: Every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels, and the only decreasing edges are the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4, each losing dimension $h$.

quote.quote: Every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels. The only decreasing edges are the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4; their dimension loss is $h$.

children.claim: The side edge from time 2 to time 5 is where the neighbor relation is used: $t_X\perp t_Y$ gives $\langle t_X\rangle\subset t_Y^\perp$, with complement $\langle t_X,t_Y\rangle^\perp$ of dimension $h-2$.

quote.quote: The side edge $2\to5$ uses the neighbor relation essentially. Since $t_X\perp t_Y$, we have $\langle t_X\rangle\subset t_Y^\perp$.

children.claim: Splitting $A=B\perp P$ and $F=\langle t\rangle\perp t^\perp$ gives every other residual, so label dimension is nondecreasing on every edge except the central $3\to4$ edges, which remove $P\otimes F\otimes Q$.

quote.quote: Label dimension is nondecreasing along every edge except center $3\to4$, which removes $P\otimes F\otimes Q$.

children.claim: The absolute label-dimension changes over all edges sum to $Wm-2N+2L$ with $L=Ich$: the signed changes telescope to the sink total $Wm-N$ minus the source total $N$, and the only exceptions to monotonicity, the $Ic$ central $3\to4$ edges, each lose $h$.
children.method: Telescope the signed changes through the gates, evaluate the two terminal sums from the prescribed labels, and add back twice the loss on the decreasing edges.

motivation.text: Absolute and signed changes differ only on decreasing edges, and the signed sum depends only on the terminal labels because each gate's label is shared by the incoming and outgoing incidence of every wire it touches.

children.claim: Each touched wire has one incoming and one outgoing incidence with the same gate label, so at every gate the signed dimension changes cancel and the signed sum telescopes to the terminal labels.

quote.quote: The signed sum of dimension changes telescopes at every gate: each touched wire has one incoming and one outgoing incidence with the same gate label.

children.claim: The source labels ($U_a$ of dimension one on the $N$ wires $X_a$, zero elsewhere) sum to $N$ and the sink labels ($U_a^\perp$ of dimension $m-1$ on the $Y_a$, $\mathcal F$ elsewhere) sum to $Wm-N$, so the signed increase is $Wm-2N$.

quote.quote: The sum of source dimensions is $N$, while the sum of sink dimensions is $Wm-N$. The signed increase is therefore $Wm-2N$.

children.claim: There are $Ic$ decreasing edges ($I=3v^2$ invocations with $c$ central wires each), each losing $h$, so $L=Ich$ and replacing signed by absolute changes adds $2L$.

quote.quote: There are $Ic$ decreasing edges, each of loss $h$; replacing signed changes by absolute changes adds $2L$.

children.claim: Over $\mathbb F_2$ every residual is nondegenerate and every nonzero one contains a norm-one vector (coordinate units outside small supports), hence is nonalternating and has an orthonormal basis, so in the complex construction a residual of dimension $k$ is realized by exactly $k$ two-point kernels, one per basis vector.

quote.quote: Each residual is nondegenerate by the decompositions above. Thus every nonzero residual is nonalternating. For completeness, every nondegenerate nonalternating binary symmetric space has an orthonormal basis.

children.claim: With $N=v^3$, $I=3v^2$, $v=\binom{100}3=161700$, $h=100$ and $c=h$ (bit) or $h+1$ (complex, the extra wire $C_\ast$), the identity $L/N=3ch/v$ gives exactly $100/539$ and $101/539$, both below $1/2$.

quote.quote: The loss ratios have the exact values \[ \frac{L_{\rm b}}{N}=\frac{100}{539},\qquad \frac{L_{\rm c}}{N}=\frac{101}{539}. \] In particular, both are smaller than $1/2$.

children.claim: With matrices $M_v=P_U$ (projection onto the label $U$ along $U^\perp$) at gates and sinks, $-P_{U_a}$ at the source of $X_a$ and $0$ at other sources, the XOR-only bit network routes each input role $w$ to $\rho(w)$ with $M_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{source}(w)}=I_m$, and its edge differences have total rational rank $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m$.
children.method: Use address shears $\Phi_M:(H,D)\mapsto(H+MD,D)$ as frames, so frames compose by adding matrices; read each edge's rank off its label change, treat the $N$ source edges separately, and telescope the terminal matrices.

motivation.text: Shear frames compose additively, $\Phi_{M'}\Phi_M=\Phi_{M'+M}$, so with $D_v=\Phi_{M_v}$ the endpoint matrix difference on each route is exactly the shear applied to that role, and each edge is a shear by a matrix of small rank.

quote.quote: Using $D_v=\Phi_{M_v}$ in \eqref{eq:common-frame-identity}, the endpoint matrix difference on each routed role is exactly the shear applied to that role.

children.claim: Each gate or sink with label $U$ gets $P_U$, the source of $X_a$ gets $-P_{U_a}$ and every other source gets $0$.

quote.quote: Assign $P_U$ to each gate or sink with label $U$. Assign the source matrix $-P_{U_a}$ to $X_a$ and zero to every other source.

children.claim: Over a radix coprime to the fixed denominators, $\Phi_M$ is an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-linear permutation of array entries with $\Phi_{M'}\Phi_M=\Phi_{M'+M}$.

quote.quote: Hence $\Phi_M$ is an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-linear permutation of array entries, and $\Phi_{M'}\Phi_M=\Phi_{M'+M}$.

children.claim: For nested nondegenerate $U\subset V$, $P_V-P_U$ is the identity on $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on its orthogonal complement, so its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$, and reversing an edge only negates it.

quote.quote: For $U\subset V$ nondegenerate, $P_V-P_U$ is the identity on $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on its orthogonal complement. Its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$; reversing the edge negates the matrix without changing its rank.

children.claim: The one exception is the $N$ edges leaving the $X_a$ sources: the first gate on $X_a$ has label $U_a$, so the edge matrix $P_{U_a}-(-P_{U_a})=2P_{U_a}$ has rank one where the label dimension did not change, adding $N$ to the label count.

quote.quote: The only exceptions are the $N$ negative source projections. At stage 1, $B=0$, and the first gate on $X_a$ has label exactly $U_a$. Its first edge matrix is therefore $2P_{U_a}$, of rational rank one, where the corresponding dimension change was zero.

children.claim: Hence $s_{\rm b}=(W_{\rm b}m-2N+2L_{\rm b})+N=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}$, whose deficit $N-2L_{\rm b}$ from $W_{\rm b}m$ is positive because $L_{\rm b}<N/2$.

quote.quote: Its deficit from $W_{\rm b}m$ is $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$.

children.claim: For $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$, and every other role has zero source and identity sink matrix, so every routed role receives the same shear $H\gets H+D$.

quote.quote: For an input $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$. Every other role has zero source matrix and identity sink matrix.

children.claim: In the complex network with binary labels and phase frames $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m}$, $q_U(x)=\operatorname{wt}(P_Ux)\bmod4$, each edge's frame change $\mathcal C_V\mathcal C_U^{-1}$ is a product of one two-point kernel $aI+bX_v$ (or its inverse) per vector of an orthonormal residual basis, these kernels number $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$, and after diagonal source and sink corrections the endpoint operator is $C^{\otimes m}$ on every role, on any number of columns.
children.method: Use additivity of Hamming weight modulo four on orthogonal binary vectors to write each frame change as one diagonal phase per residual basis vector, conjugate each phase by Hadamard matrices into a translation kernel, and telescope the frames along each route, repairing the one route $X_a\to Y_a$ with $Z$ signs.

motivation.text: The frames are chosen so that the endpoint operator becomes the butterfly layer after diagonal phases and a dyadic scale, while each edge is a few smaller calls of the same procedure on fewer selected bits.

quote.quote: For the numerical procedure, the endpoint operator becomes the simultaneous $H_0$ layer after diagonal phase operations and a dyadic scale. The intermediate frames are chosen so that every edge can be implemented by smaller calls to the same procedure.

children.claim: Since $\operatorname{wt}(z+w)=\operatorname{wt}(z)+\operatorname{wt}(w)-2|\operatorname{supp}(z)\cap\operatorname{supp}(w)|$, weight is additive modulo four when $z\cdot w=0$, so on an increasing edge $q_V-q_U\equiv\sum_{v\in\mathcal B}\operatorname{wt}(v)[v\cdot x]\pmod4$ for an orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$ of the residual, with the sign reversed on a decreasing edge.

quote.quote: If $z\cdot w=0$, the intersection cardinality is even, so weight is additive modulo four.

children.claim: Each basis vector has odd weight, so its phase is $i^{\varepsilon[v\cdot x]}=\frac{1+i^\varepsilon}2+\frac{1-i^\varepsilon}2(-1)^{v\cdot x}$, and $H\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)H=X$ turns the character into the translation $X_v$, giving $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

quote.quote: The displayed phase therefore becomes $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

children.claim: Nonzero residuals have orthonormal bases and zero residuals take the empty basis, so the kernels number $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}$, with deficit $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$ and no source exception.

quote.quote: The nonzero residuals have such bases by Lemma~\ref{lem:motif-residuals}; for a zero residual use the empty basis. The same lemma gives the count $s_{\rm c}$. The deficit is $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$.

children.claim: On $k$ columns every frame is a $k$th tensor power, so each residual vector contributes one factor acting on all $k$ columns at once.

quote.quote: Thus each residual vector contributes one factor acting on all $k$ columns, and there are $s_{\rm c}$ such factors over the network.

children.claim: The zero label has frame $I$ and the full label frame $C^{\otimes m}$ since $q_{\mathcal F}(x)=\operatorname{wt}(x)$, so every route except $X_a\to Y_a$ already receives $C^{\otimes m}$.

quote.quote: The zero label has frame $I$, while the full label has frame $C^{\otimes m}$ because $q_{\mathcal F}(x)=\operatorname{wt}(x)$. Every pair except $X_a\to Y_a$ has these zero and full labels.

children.claim: On the exceptional route $X_a\to Y_a$ the operator is $C^{-1}$ on the 27 coordinates of $\operatorname{supp}(u_a)$ and $C$ elsewhere; applying $Z_{a,k}$ before and $i^{27k}Z_{a,k}$ after turns all $27k$ inverse factors into $C$ by $C=iZC^{-1}Z$.

quote.quote: There are $27k$ inverse factors, so the identity $C=iZC^{-1}Z$ turns each of them into $C$.

children.claim: Negating the physical $X$ outputs and returning output role $\rho(w)$ to role $w$ leaves the forward tensor product on every role, scratch roles included.

quote.quote: Every role, including every scratch role, now has the required forward tensor product.

children.claim: The relative deficits $\eta_{\rm b}=339/22587335000000$ and $\eta_{\rm c}=73/19906842167500$ both exceed $20\cdot2^{-50}$, and $\log m<20$ gives $m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20\cdot2^{-50})>m(1-\eta)$, so $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$ and $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^\sigma$ with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$.

quote.quote: Both exact deficits displayed above are greater than $20\cdot2^{-50}$. Since $m<2^{20}$ and $\log 2<1$, we have $\log m<20$, whence \[ m^{1-2^{-50}} =m\exp(-2^{-50}\log m) >m(1-20\cdot2^{-50})>m(1-\eta) \] for either $\eta=\eta_{\rm b}$ or $\eta=\eta_{\rm c}$. Consequently \[ \frac{s_{\rm b}}{W_{\rm b}}<m^\tau, \qquad \frac{s_{\rm c}}{W_{\rm c}}<m^\sigma, \qquad 0<\tau=\sigma<1.

children.claim: One fixed-tape procedure transforms any bit array on $[P]\times[2^u]\times[G]\times[2^u]\times[B]$ by exchanging its two $u$-bit address coordinates while fixing the prefix, gap and suffix coordinates, in $O(Vu^\tau)$ steps with $\tau=1-2^{-50}$, for arbitrary prefix, gap and suffix lengths, padding and cleanup included.
children.method: Pad the chunks numerically to radix-$q$ ranges $[q^e]$, supply a row field from the top $O(\log e)$ digits of both chunks and pad its count to a multiple of $W^k$, write the remaining width in base $m$ and interchange corresponding pieces by the power-width procedure, then undo the joins and the padding.

motivation.text: The power-width procedure needs widths that are powers of $m$ and a row field divisible by $W^k$; a few high digits of the chunks supply the rows cheaply, and a base-$m$ split of the width makes the piece costs a geometric sum.

quote.quote: Rows for a general array can be supplied by a few of its own high digits. Their movement will cost less than the final bound.

children.salient: The final effect is an exact permutation, valid for arbitrary initial auxiliary values, although intermediate steps form XOR combinations of data, and it costs $O(Vu^\tau)$ rather than the $\Theta(Vu)$ of moving one digit at a time.

adds.name: chunk digit width
adds.meaning: The number of radix-q digits in each of the two chunks being interchanged.

adds.name: recursion depth
adds.meaning: The number of recursion levels, the exponent with e equal to m to the power k.

children.claim: For a fixed circuit with $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$ and $s<Wm$ and a rational $\tau$ with $s/W<m^\tau$, two disjoint chunks of $e=m^k$ radix-$q$ digits can be interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time whenever a row field before both chunks has length divisible by $W^k$.
children.method: Write each chunk as $m$ fields of $e/m$ digits ($H$ and $D$), split rows cyclically into $W$ role streams, run the bit network with frames $\Phi_{M_v}$ so that each edge is a matrix shear done by recursive interchanges of smaller fields, merge to get $H\gets H+D$ on every row, compose three shears into the interchange, and solve the volume-normalized recurrence.

motivation.text: Each edge matrix of rank $a$ costs $a$ smaller interchanges, and the ranks sum to less than $W$ times $m$, so the recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.

quote.quote: Because the sum of these ranks is less than the number of wires times $m$, the resulting recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.

children.claim: For a fixed finite set of rational $m\times m$ matrices there is a fixed odd prime $q$ such that, for fields over $[q^b]$ with every $H_i$ before every $D_j$, the permutation $(H,D)\mapsto(H+AD,D)$ over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$ with $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}A=a$ takes exactly $a$ interchanges of $b$-digit fields plus $O(V)$ further work.
children.method: Factor $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ once and for all, pick $q$ avoiding all denominators and diagonal numerators, perform the triangular parts as controlled updates of later fields by earlier ones, and realize each one of $\Pi$ by two such updates around one interchange.

motivation.text: Controlled shifts update a later field from earlier ones in linear time, and lower-triangular coordinate changes only ever update in that direction, so all of a shear except its rank-many pivots is linear-time work.

quote.quote: Lemma~\ref{lem:ordered-affine-streams} updates a later field using earlier fields in linear time. Lower triangular changes of coordinates can be performed entirely in this direction.

children.claim: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ factors as $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with $E_1,E_2$ invertible lower triangular and $\Pi$ a partial permutation matrix with exactly $a$ ones (a Bruhat factorization with coordinate order reversed).
children.method: Eliminate from the topmost nonzero row at its rightmost nonzero entry, clearing the row to the left by lower-triangular column operations and the column below by lower-triangular row operations, and repeat on the remaining indices.

motivation.text: Choosing the topmost row and its rightmost entry means all clearing goes leftward and downward, so every elementary operation is lower triangular in the original order.

children.claim: At the topmost nonzero row's rightmost nonzero entry, the entries to its left are cleared by right multiplication and those below by left multiplication with lower triangular elementary matrices, since rows above are zero in the active columns.

quote.quote: Otherwise choose the topmost nonzero row and its rightmost nonzero entry. Use that pivot column to clear entries to its left by right multiplication by lower triangular elementary matrices. There are no nonzero entries to its right in the pivot row. Clear entries below the pivot by left multiplication by lower triangular elementary matrices, and scale the pivot to one. All rows above the chosen row were zero in the still active columns.

children.claim: Each pivot isolates a rank-one block, so the resulting $LAR=\Pi$ has exactly $a$ ones, and $E_1=L^{-1}$, $E_2=R^{-1}$ are invertible lower triangular.

quote.quote: Each step isolates a rank-one block and leaves the remaining rank in the active submatrix. Thus the final partial permutation matrix has exactly $a$ ones. If $LAR=\Pi$ is the resulting identity, then $E_1=L^{-1}$ and $E_2=R^{-1}$ have the required form.

children.claim: A lower-triangular transformation of $H$ or $D$ costs $O(V)$: update coordinates in descending physical order, multiplying by the diagonal unit and adding a fixed combination of earlier coordinates, which still hold their original values.

quote.quote: A lower triangular transformation of $H$, or of $D$, costs $O(V)$: update coordinates in descending physical order.

children.claim: Each one of $\Pi$ at $(i,j)$, i.e. $H_i\gets H_i+D_j$, is done as $D_j\gets D_j+H_i$, $(H_i,D_j)\gets(D_j,H_i)$, $D_j\gets H_i-D_j$, taking $(h,d)$ to $(h+d,d)$ with one interchange, so the shear uses exactly $a$ interchanges.

quote.quote: On an initial pair $(h,d)$ this sequence yields $(h+d,d)$. It uses just one interchange. There are $a$ ones, which proves the claim.

children.claim: The bit network supplies the required finite data: $W=W_{\rm b}$ wires, terminal and gate matrices with $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$, and edge-rank sum $s=s_{\rm b}<Wm$ with the negative source projections counted.

quote.quote: Proposition~\ref{prop:bit-motif-interface} supplies these conditions with $W=W_{\rm b}$ and $s=s_{\rm b}$. Its negative source projection is essential to the endpoint identity and has already been included in the rank sum.

children.claim: Splitting whole rows cyclically within each prefix, row $Wg+(w-1)$ going to role stream $w$ as row $g$, gives $W$ streams of identical shape, each of volume $V/W$ with row count divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

quote.quote: These streams have exactly the same remaining shape, including the full ranges of $H$ and $D$. Each has logical volume $V/W$, and its row count is divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

children.claim: Each circuit edge applies $\Phi_{A_e}$, $A_e=M_{\mathrm{head}(e)}-M_{\mathrm{tail}(e)}$, to its role stream by the matrix-shear lemma with recursive interchanges of the pivot pairs of $(e/m)$-digit fields, and each gate acts pointwise at matching addresses.

quote.quote: On every circuit edge apply $\Phi_{A_e}$ to that role stream; implement it by Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-shear}, recursively interchanging each pivot pair of $b$-digit fields.

children.claim: A common address permutation commutes with pointwise bit gates, so the frame identity gives $f'_{\rho(w)}=\Phi_{M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}}\Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w=\Phi_{I_m}f_w$ on every role.

quote.quote: The same invariant proof applies because a common address permutation commutes with every pointwise bit gate.

children.claim: Merging row $g$ of output role $\rho(w)$ back to row $Wg+(w-1)$ undoes $\rho$ and yields $H\gets H+D$ on every original row, including rows that served as scratch with arbitrary values.

quote.quote: The result is $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every original row, including rows assigned to scratch roles, whose initial values were arbitrary.

children.claim: The componentwise updates $D\gets D-H$, $H\gets H+D$, $D\gets H-D$ send $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$; only the middle shear uses the circuit, the other two update the later group in linear time.

quote.quote: Only the middle shear uses the circuit. The other two updates target the later group and have linear cost. The transformation sends $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$.

children.claim: The procedure makes exactly $s$ recursive calls, each on a role stream of volume $V/W$ with chunks $m$ times narrower, plus $O(V)$ other work, so the normalized cost obeys $F_0=O(1)$, $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, and $s/W<m^\tau$ gives $F_k=O(e^\tau)$ for $e=m^k$.
children.method: Count the recursive calls as the sum of edge ranks, divide time by logical volume, and sum the resulting geometric series.

motivation.text: Dividing cost by volume turns $s$ children of volume $V/W$ into the factor $s/W$, which is below $m^\tau$; a geometric series with that ratio is dominated by $m^{k\tau}=e^\tau$ (or by $k+1$ when the ratio is at most one).

quote.quote: A recursive call at parameter $mf$ therefore uses $s$ calls at parameter $f$, each on a stream of volume $V/W$.

children.salient: Each level multiplies the chunk width by $m$ but the normalized cost only by $s/W<m^\tau$, so the cost grows like $e^\tau$ with $\tau<1$ rather than linearly in the width.

adds.name: normalized cost
adds.meaning: A uniform bound on running time divided by logical volume for chunks of m^k digits.

children.claim: The number of recursive calls is the sum $s$ of the edge ranks, and each acts on one role stream of volume $V/W$ with all other fields as spectators.

quote.quote: The number of recursive calls is the sum of the edge ranks, exactly $s$. Each acts on one role stream of volume $V/W$, retaining all other fields as spectators.

children.claim: With ratio $s/W<m^\tau$, $\sum_{j\le k}(s/W)^j$ is $k+1=O(m^{k\tau})$ when $s/W\le1$ and $O((s/W)^k)$ otherwise, so $F_k=O(m^{k\tau})=O(e^\tau)$.

quote.quote: For $a=s/W<m^\tau$ the geometric sum $\sum_{j=0}^k a^j$ is $O(m^{k\tau})$. If $a\le1$, the sum is at most $k+1=O(m^{k\tau})$; if $a>1$, it is $O(a^k)$. Hence $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

children.claim: On fixed tapes, parking the $W-1$ inactive streams on a stack, copying the active one to the child and restoring afterwards moves $O(V)$ symbols per child, and there are only $s$ children, so scheduling adds $O(V)$ per node and no factor to $s/W$.

quote.quote: Each push, pop, copy, positioning operation, or erasure moves $O(V)$ symbols at a parent node. There are only the fixed number $s$ of child calls.

children.claim: For chunks of $e$ radix-$q$ digits, interchanging the top $\lceil k\log W/(2\log q)\rceil=O(\log e)$ digits pairwise and joining them gives a row field of range at least $W^k$ before both remaining chunks, at cost $O(V\log e)$; zero rows pad its count to a multiple of $W^k$, less than doubling the volume.

quote.quote: The joining moves preserve the order of the remaining digits and the gap field. Exchanging and joining the high parts costs $O(V\rho)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:elementary-streams}.

children.claim: Writing the remaining width as $\sum_{j\le k}a_jm^j$ with $0\le a_j<m$ and interchanging the $a_j$ pairs of width-$m^j$ pieces on the common padded row field costs $O(V)\sum_ja_jm^{j\tau}=O(Ve^\tau)$, a geometric sum since $a_j<m$ and $m^k<me$, and each call preserves row addresses so padded rows stay zero.

quote.quote: The fixed bound $a_j<m$ and the inequality $m^k<me$ make this a geometric sum of the stated order.

children.claim: Binary chunks of $u$ bits are padded numerically to $[q^e]$ with $q^e\ge2^u$ (a fixed factor below $q^2$ in volume), which keeps entry order because radix-$q$ lexicographic order is numerical order; invalid entries are scanned away after the interchange, and $e=O(u)$ gives $O(Vu^\tau)$.

quote.quote: Lexicographic radix-$q$ order of $[q^e]$ is its numerical order, just as binary order of $[2^u]$ is its numerical order. Padding therefore preserves the order of the existing entries without converting the digits of every address. The completed interchange preserves the set on which both chunk coordinates lie below $2^u$. Scan away the other entries to recover the desired binary array. Since $e=O(u)$ for fixed $q$, the bound is $O(Vu^\tau)$.

children.claim: For large $p$, $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$, $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$ and $r=2^{\Theta(p/d)}$, one fixed-tape procedure applies the tensor product $\mathcal H$ of $H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2)$ at bit $\rho$ of each of $D\le d$ consecutive $K$-bit address chunks to arrays of $r$-coefficient disk-grid polynomial records, returning $Q_p(\mathcal Hz)$, within $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ of $\mathcal Hz$, in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time, exact before one final truncation.
children.method: Express $C^{\otimes e}$ through the complex network's phase frames on $m$ slots with each edge a binary basis change around smaller calls, implement basis changes by packed selected-bit additions, supply rows from the first chunks and split them among the $W$ roles, solve the recurrence, bound the exact dyadic growth, and convert $C^{\otimes D}$ to $H_0^{\otimes D}$ by diagonal phases and a scale.

motivation.text: Applying the $D$ butterfly factors separately would cost $D$ whole-array passes; the network processes all selected bits together with a power saving.

quote.quote: We will obtain cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with $\lambda'<1$ and $V$ the logical bit volume, whereas separate butterfly factors would require $D$ whole-array passes.

adds.name: group chunk count
adds.meaning: The number of selected chunks handled by one recursive call of the layer construction.

adds.name: active chunk count
adds.meaning: The number of consecutive chunks whose selected bits one layer transforms, at most d.

adds.name: slot width
adds.meaning: The number of chunks in one slot, equal to the number of selected bits one child call or one packed addition handles.

adds.name: two-point phase kernel
adds.meaning: The two-by-two matrix aI+bX with a=(1+i)/2 and b=(1-i)/2 given by the complex network's phase interface.

adds.name: butterfly layer
adds.meaning: The tensor product of the normalized butterfly over the selected bits, acting coefficientwise on the records.

children.claim: On a group of $e=mf$ selected chunks arranged as $m$ slots of $f$ chunks, the complex network with column frames $\mathcal C_U^{\otimes f}$ yields $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role using exactly $s_{\rm c}$ child calls $C^{\otimes f}$ on single slots, a fixed number of binary row additions and coefficientwise scalar operations, and $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ with exact Gaussian dyadic phases.
children.method: Conjugate each edge's directional kernels into coordinate directions by an address permutation $\mathcal P_M$ whose matrix extends the residual basis, run one child per direction on one slot, realize inverse kernels and endpoint corrections by signs and fourth-root phases, and convert $C$ to $H_0$ by diagonal phases.

motivation.text: A child call acts on whole slots of coordinate bits, so each residual direction must first be moved into a coordinate position; an invertible binary change of basis does this without a general transpose.

quote.quote: The next step puts those directions into coordinate positions without performing a general transpose.

children.claim: Taking a basis extending the residual basis as the columns of $M$ gives $\mathcal C_{U_+}\mathcal C_{U_-}^{-1}=\mathcal P_M(\prod_jC_{e_j}^{\epsilon_j})\mathcal P_M^{-1}$, which uses only $\mathcal P_MX_v\mathcal P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv}$ and the invertibility of $M$.

quote.quote: The matrix $M$ need not preserve the dot product: equation~\eqref{eq:phase-conjugation} only uses its invertibility.

children.claim: An inverse kernel needs one forward child, since $(C^{-1})^{\otimes f}=(-i)^fZ^{\otimes f}C^{\otimes f}Z^{\otimes f}$ with address signs and fourth-root phases as wrappers.

quote.quote: A negative directional kernel still requires only one forward child, because \begin{equation}\label{eq:phase-inverse-child} (C^{-1})^{\otimes f} =(-i)^f Z^{\otimes f}C^{\otimes f}Z^{\otimes f}. \end{equation} The rightmost phase is applied first. All inverse wrappers are address signs and constant fourth-root phases, so they add no recursive calls.

children.claim: Each $\mathcal P_M$ is at most $m(m-1)+3m$ row additions, each XORing the selected bits of one whole slot into the corresponding bits of another.

quote.quote: Gaussian elimination expresses any $M\in\operatorname{GL}(m,\mathbb F_2)$ as a product of at most $m(m-1)+3m$ elementary row additions: one clears at most $m-1$ other entries per pivot, and each row swap is three row additions. Reversing the elimination gives the required product since each row addition is an involution. The number is a constant because $m$ is fixed. Adding row $h'$ to row $h$ in every column applies $x_{h,j}\leftarrow x_{h,j}\mathbin\oplus x_{h',j}$ for every $0\le j<f$. Thus one row addition changes corresponding selected positions in two whole slots.

children.claim: Summing residual dimensions gives exactly $s_{\rm c}$ child calls, each on the $f$ chunks of one slot, and the phase interface gives $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role.

quote.quote: Summing its residual dimensions gives exactly $s_{\rm c}$ child calls, each on the $f=e/m$ axes of one slot.

children.claim: Since $H_0=b\mathsf SC\mathsf S$ with $\mathsf S=\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$, $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$, and $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}$ is a binary shift and a fourth-root phase with at most one further factor $b$.

quote.quote: The scalar is \[ b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}, \] so it is a binary shift and fourth-root phase, with at most one further factor $b$.

children.claim: For $R$-bit records on $[N_0]\times[2^L]_{\chi_1}\times[N_1]\times[2^L]_{\chi_2}\times[N_2]\times[2^L]_{\chi_3}\times[N_3]$ with $L=fK$, one fixed procedure performs $y_{j_i}\gets y_{j_i}\oplus x_{j_i}$ at the selected positions $j_i=\rho+iK$, $0\le i<f$, restoring the scratch chunk $z$ for every initial value, in $O(V(L^\tau+1))$ time when $R$ exceeds every fixed polynomial in $p$ and $K/\log p\to\infty$.
children.method: Apply eight cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges, each adding to all $K$-bit segments at once, which flip the parity of each $y$ segment exactly when its control bit is one and restore $z$; they agree with the ideal XOR map off an explicit set $\mathcal B$ of addresses with extreme guard values, which is then repaired by extracting, sorting and reinserting those records.

motivation.text: A shift of a whole chunk range adds to every segment of the chunk at once, so packed integer additions handle all selected bits together; carries between segments occur only at addresses with extreme guard values, few enough when $K/\log p\to\infty$ to repair by sorting.

quote.quote: Also $K/\log p\to\infty$, which will make the exceptional set in a packed change of address bits small enough to repair by sorting.

children.salient: Eight cyclic shifts, each a bijection, net to flipping the parity of $u$ exactly when $c=1$ while restoring the arbitrary scratch integer $w$, and the repair depends only on addresses, so the bound is worst case over all payloads.

children.claim: For a control $c$ and integers $u,w$, the eight conditional $\pm1$ updates induce $(00\ 01\ 10)$ and then $(01\ 10\ 11)$ on parity squares, composing to $(00\ 10)(01\ 11)$, i.e. $(u',w')=(u+c(1-2(u\bmod2)),w)$: the parity of $u$ flips exactly when $c=1$, both quotients by two are kept and $w$ is restored.

quote.quote: Applying the first cycle and then the second gives $(00\ 10)(01\ 11)$.

children.claim: Applied to the $K$-bit segments starting at $j_0,\dots,j_{f-2}$, each line is one cyclic shift $y\gets y+\varepsilon\sum_i2^{j_i}[x_{j_i}=1][z_{j_i}=b]\pmod{2^L}$ whose offset does not depend on its target, hence a bijection of the rectangle.

quote.quote: Physically, a line updating $y$ by sign $\varepsilon$ and testing parity $b$ of $z$ is the single cyclic shift \begin{equation} \label{eq:packed-cyclic-shift} y\longleftarrow y+ \varepsilon\sum_{i=0}^{f-2}2^{j_i} [\,x_{j_i}=1\,][\,z_{j_i}=b\,] \pmod{2^L}. \end{equation} For a line updating $z$, interchange $y$ and $z$ in this formula. The shift offset never depends on its target chunk, so each line is a bijection of the rectangle.

children.claim: Off the set $\mathcal B$ of addresses where some used guard value fails $10\le g\le2^{K-1}-11$, each segment starts in $[20,2^K-21]$ and moves by at most eight, so no segment carries into the next and the composition $S_0$ agrees with the ideal XOR map $T_0$.

quote.quote: Inductively, each packed addition therefore agrees with all the independent segment additions: no segment carries into or borrows from the next segment.

children.claim: Each guard excludes exactly twenty of its $2^{K-1}$ values, so a union bound over the $2(f-1)$ guards gives $|\mathcal B|\le\min\{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}\}M$, whatever the record payloads.

quote.quote: There are exactly twenty excluded values for each guard in \eqref{eq:packed-guard-interval}. Since its complete range has $2^{K-1}$ values, the union bound over the $2(f-1)$ guards gives \begin{equation} \label{eq:packed-bad-fraction} |\mathcal B|\le\delta_{\rm bad}M.

children.claim: Since $T_0$ preserves guard values, $S_0$ and $T_0$ are bijections agreeing off $\mathcal B$, so $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fixes the complement of $\mathcal B$ and permutes $\mathcal B$; the exceptional records are extracted with their destination ranks, radix sorted and reinserted.

quote.quote: Thus $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fixes $\mathcal B^c$ and permutes $\mathcal B$. It remains to implement the rotations and this correction on tapes.

children.claim: The omitted top position $j_{f-1}$ is one two-bit XOR in $O(V)$, and for $f=1$ this is the whole algorithm.

quote.quote: Finally apply the two-bit XOR to $x_{j_{f-1}},y_{j_{f-1}}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:elementary-streams}, splitting those chunks at the selected positions and collapsing the other intervals. Its descriptor again has a fixed number of positive lengths, each at most $V$. This costs $O(V)$ and supplies the omitted selected position. When $f=1$, $S_0,T_0$ are identities, $\mathcal B$ is empty, and this last step is the entire algorithm.

children.claim: The shifts cost $O(V(L^\tau+1))$ through at most sixteen interchanges and eight rotations, and with $A=\lceil\log_2(2V)\rceil=O(p)$ the repair terms per unit volume, $A^3/R$ and $80(f-1)2^{-K}A(1+A/R)$, tend to zero under the family bounds.

quote.quote: Under the stated family bounds the first tends to zero, and the second is $O(p^2 2^{-K}(1+A_{\rm rect}/R))=o(1)$. This proves the final assertion.

children.claim: A row addition of a binary change of basis is one packed selected-bit addition with slot $h'$ as $x$, slot $h$ as $y$ and a third slot as $z$, so a whole change of basis and its inverse on a stream of volume $V$ cost $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$.

quote.quote: To add row $h'$ to row $h$, use slot $h'$ as $x$, slot $h$ as $y$, and any third, distinct slot as $z$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:packed-selected-bit-rectangle}. The lemma performs $x_{h,j}\leftarrow x_{h,j}\mathbin\oplus x_{h',j}$ for every $j$ in one operation and restores the third slot, whatever its initial address value.

children.claim: With rows supplied by the first chunks and split among the $W$ roles, the normalized cost $F(e)$ of $C^{\otimes e}$ obeys $F(e)\le(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1)$ for $e\ge d^{1/2}$ and $F(e)=O(e)$ below, which over the base-$m$ pieces of the active chunks gives $O(d^{\lambda'})$ for any fixed $\lambda'$ with $\max\{\lambda,\sigma+(1-\sigma)/2\}<\lambda'<1$.
children.method: Charge each internal node its basis changes, gates and corrections, give each of its $s$ children $1/W$ of the volume, stop with individual kernels when fewer than $d^{1/2}$ chunks remain, and sum internal and leaf contributions.

motivation.text: Splitting complete rows among the wire roles divides each recursive call's volume by $W$, which turns the $s$ children into the factor $s/W\le m^\sigma$ per level.

quote.quote: Splitting complete rows among the network's wire roles then reduces the volume of each recursive call.

children.claim: One kernel $C(u,v)=((u+v+i(u-v))/2,(u+v-i(u-v))/2)$ at a selected bit is a split, an exact paired coefficient scan and a merge, $O(V)$, so $e$ individual kernels cost $O(Ve)$.

quote.quote: Thus \(e\) individual kernels cost \(O(Ve)\) on any stream with these complete ranges and record format.

children.claim: An internal node with $e=m^k$ chunks makes exactly $s$ calls on slots, one per residual basis vector, and its other work costs $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$.

quote.quote: The phase construction supplies one recursive call on a slot for each vector in an edge residual basis, hence exactly \(s\) calls in one invocation of the network.

children.claim: After individual kernels on the first $q_0=\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ chunks, their bits form a row index of range $2^{q_0K}\ge W^{\lceil\log_md\rceil}$, padded with zero rows to a multiple of that power at most doubling the volume.

quote.quote: Its range has length \(R_{\rm row}=2^{q_0K}\ge W^{k_0}\), since \(K\ge1\) for sufficiently large \(p\) and \(q_0K\ge k_0\log_2W\).

children.claim: Sending row $Wg+w$ to role $w$ gives role streams of identical shape, so pointwise gates align, existing rows supply the scratch roles, and each child has exactly $1/W$ of its parent's volume.

quote.quote: Each recursive edge call acts on one role stream with volume exactly \(1/W\) of its parent's logical volume.

children.claim: The $s$ children on volume $V/W$ cost $s(V/W)F(e/m)$, giving the factor $s/W$, and at internal nodes $K\le e^{2c}$ makes the overhead $O(e^\lambda)$.

quote.quote: Indeed, the \(s\) child calls are executed on streams of volume \(V/W\), so their total cost is \(s(V/W)F(e/m)\).

children.claim: Since $s/W\le m^\sigma<m^\lambda$, the internal costs sum to $O(e^\lambda)$ as a geometric series, and leaves after $j$ levels with $u<d^{1/2}$ chunks contribute $O((s/W)^ju)\le O(e^\sigma u^{1-\sigma})\le O(e^\sigma d^{(1-\sigma)/2})$.

quote.quote: Put \(a=s/W\). Since \(a\le m^\sigma<m^\lambda\), the internal costs sum to at most \[ C e^\lambda\sum_{j\ge0}(a/m^\lambda)^j=O(e^\lambda).

children.claim: Splitting the $D-q_0$ remaining chunks into base-$m$ pieces of $m^j$ chunks, at most $(m-1)(1+\lfloor\log_md\rfloor)$ of them, and adding the row preprocessing gives $O(\log(2d)[d^\lambda+d^{\sigma+(1-\sigma)/2}+1])=O(d^{\lambda'})$.

quote.quote: Write \(D-q_0=\sum_j a_jm^j\) in base \(m\), with \(0\le a_j<m\). Partition the remaining chunks into \(a_j\) consecutive pieces containing \(m^j\) chunks for each \(j\). There are at most \((m-1)(1+\lfloor\log_m d\rfloor)\) pieces.

children.claim: Every intermediate coefficient of one layer is an exact Gaussian dyadic whose denominator and magnitude growth are bounded by $\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil$ with $C_0=128m(s+64(W+m+1)^3)^2$ and $C_1=20$, so $p+\Delta$ fractional and $\Delta+3$ integer bits represent the whole layer exactly, and $\epsilon C_1<1$ makes $\Delta=o(p)$ and the width $O(p)$.
children.method: Bound the arithmetic dependency depth by $A(e)\le sA(e/m)+E$ at internal nodes and $A(e)\le8e$ at leaves, add the outer phases and the final shift, and note that each operation at most doubles the modulus and adds one denominator bit.

motivation.text: The intermediate network operators are not contractions, so instead of truncating along the way the whole layer is evaluated exactly, which requires a bound on the growth of denominators and magnitudes.

quote.quote: The accelerated network is evaluated exactly until an entire normalized butterfly layer is complete. Its intermediate operators need not be contractions.

children.claim: One invocation adds fewer than $E=64(W+m+1)^3$ operations to any dependency chain (at most $12W$ gates of at most $2W^2$ operations, plus child and endpoint corrections), so $A(e)\le sA(e/m)+E$ and, through $\lceil\log_md\rceil$ levels, $A(e)\le8B^2d^{\nu+1}$ with $B=s+E$ and $\nu$ the least $j$ with $m^j\ge B$.

quote.quote: Since \(s<Wm\), the total \(24W^3+4s+4W+4\) is less than \(E=64(W+m+1)^3\).

children.claim: A value at depth $t$ lies in $2^{-(p+t)}\mathbb Z[i]$ with modulus at most $2^t$, since addition at most doubles the modulus, halving adds one denominator bit, and signs and multiplication by $i$ change neither.

quote.quote: This follows by induction: addition or subtraction can at most double the maximum modulus of its operands; halving adds at most one denominator bit; and signs and multiplication by \(i\) preserve both bounds.

children.claim: With $\epsilon C_1<1$ and $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$, $\Delta=o(p)$, so the full coefficient width is $O(p)$ as the time analysis assumes.

quote.quote: Choose \(\epsilon C_1<1\). Since \(d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)\), \(\Delta=o(p)\), and the full coefficient width is \(O(p)\), as required in the time analysis.

children.claim: With $d,r$ in fixed bands, $K\ge6$, $K/\log p\to\infty$ and $r$ exceeds every fixed power of $p$, so every packed call meets its family bounds with one common time constant.

quote.quote: Thus Lemma~\ref{lem:packed-selected-bit-rectangle} has the required $O(M_{\rm child}R_{\rm g}(L^\tau+1))$ cost for every packed call, with one common time constant.

children.claim: Every row of $\mathcal H$ has absolute row sum one, so $\mathcal H$ maps disk arrays to disk arrays, and the single final truncation toward zero keeps the disk and adds error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.

quote.quote: Thus $\mathcal H$ maps disk arrays to disk arrays, and componentwise truncation preserves that disk and has error less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$: truncation cannot increase the absolute value of either component, and changes each by less than $2^{-p}$.

children.claim: Placed inside the reduction of multiplication to synthetic polynomial transforms, with every change of representation, precision loss and tape movement accounted for, the two procedures yield the exact $2n$-bit product in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time.
children.method: Compute normalized convolution over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ by synthetic transforms in a retained layout, express the prime-length source transforms through power-of-two transforms by Gaussian resampling and the chirp identity while keeping both coordinate permutations in the formulas, and assemble the algorithm: digits, Chinese-remainder address map, coefficient twist, source transforms, pointwise product, opposite transform, rounding and carries.

motivation.text: Once one coordinate is a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, roots of unity are signed shifts, so the transforms consist only of address rearrangements, signed shifts and two-point butterflies, which is exactly what the two tape procedures accelerate.

quote.quote: In this representation, the transform calculation consists of address rearrangements, signed shifts, and two-point butterfly operations.

adds.name: padded box size
adds.meaning: The number of entries of the padded power-of-two transform box, the product of the axis lengths.

adds.name: ring log-length
adds.meaning: The base-two logarithm of r, so every axis has length 2^ell or 2^{ell-1}.

adds.name: record count
adds.meaning: The number T/r of polynomial records in a ring array, the product of all axis lengths but the last.

adds.name: Gaussian width
adds.meaning: The integer parameter, between 2 and the square root of p, that sets the width of the Gaussian kernels.

adds.name: resampling scale exponent
adds.meaning: The exponent 2d alpha^2 of the power of two that rescales the normalized resampled transform.

adds.name: prime source length
adds.meaning: The odd prime length of source axis i, coprime to the power of two t_i.

children.claim: Normalized convolution $\mathcal M_r(f,g)=(f*g)/T$ of disk-grid arrays of $M=T/r$ records in $\mathcal R_r$ is computed with error below $\sqrt2M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$ in time $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}+\log(rp)])$, by two forward synthetic transforms, pointwise normalized ring products, and the opposite transform consuming the same stored order, followed by an exact scale $M$.
children.method: Perform both forward transforms and keep their common stored order $LB$, multiply corresponding records by signed packing, apply the opposite procedure to that order, scale exactly by $M$, and compare with the exact identity through contraction bounds.

motivation.text: Pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the same record permutation to both operands, so the forward outputs can be multiplied in their stored order and passed straight to the opposite transform, with no reordering.

quote.quote: Pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the same record permutation $LB$ to both operands. We may therefore multiply the forward outputs in their retained order and pass that order directly to the opposite procedure.

children.claim: For $d-1$ axes of lengths $t_i\in\{2^{\ell-1},2^\ell\}$ with records in $\mathcal R_r$, a fixed-tape forward procedure with exact counterpart $LBF_{\boldsymbol t}^-$ and an opposite procedure consuming that order with exact counterpart $F_{\boldsymbol t}^+B^{-1}L^{-1}$ ($B$ the bit-reversal order, $L$ a layout permutation) each have error below $\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$ and cost $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$.
children.method: Move the leading slot of each long axis and the lowest $(\ell-1)\bmod K$ slots of every axis to a prefix, interchange the remaining $K$-bit chunks into chunk-index-major order, run each round on the remaining chunks as one simultaneous layer followed by an exact monomial twiddle, process prefix rounds individually, and truncate once per round.

motivation.text: A simultaneous layer needs the selected bits of all participating axes at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks, which the layout provides once for all rounds.

quote.quote: To apply Proposition~\ref{prop:simultaneous-layer} in a transform round, we must place the selected bits of the participating axes at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

children.claim: With $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$ in $\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$, the normalized transforms $F_t^\pm$ are contractions with $F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I$, the decimation-in-frequency recursion computes $B_tF_t^-$ with outputs in bit-reversed slots, the reversed recursion computes $F_t^+B_t^{-1}$, and on several axes each round is a parallel butterfly followed by one address-determined monomial $y^E$.
children.method: Verify character cancellation directly in a ring with zero divisors, follow the address-bit slots through the decimation-in-frequency recursion (butterfly $H_0$, then twiddle $\omega_t^{-k}$ on one branch), and invert the levels using $H_0^2=I/2$.

motivation.text: In $\mathcal R_r$ the roots of unity are powers of $y$, which act by exact signed permutations of coefficient lists, so twiddles cost no arithmetic and only the butterflies do.

quote.quote: Their entries will be short polynomials in a quotient where the required roots of unity act by exact signed permutations of coefficient lists.

children.salient: All roots of unity are exact: multiplying by a power of $\omega_t$ is a signed cyclic shift of the coefficient list, so the butterflies are the only arithmetic, and outputs land in bit-reversed order without moving any frequency index.

children.claim: Every power of $\omega_t$ is an isometry of the coefficient sup norm and each transform entry averages $t$ such images, so $F_t^-$ and $F_t^+$ are contractions.

quote.quote: Every power of $\omega_t$ is an isometry, and each transform entry is an average of $t$ such images. Thus both transforms are contractions.

children.claim: $\sum_k\omega_t^{jk}$ is $t$ if $t\mid j$ and $0$ otherwise, because shifting $k$ by $t/2^{v+1}$ multiplies the sum by $y^{rj_0}=-1$ and the additive group has no two-torsion; hence $F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I$.

quote.quote: Replacing $k$ by $k+t/2^{v+1}$ modulo $t$ permutes the summands and multiplies their sum by $y^{rj_0}=-1$. Hence the sum is zero, since the additive group of $\mathcal R_r$ has no two-torsion.

children.claim: After all $\log_2t$ levels the entry $(F_t^-z)_j$ sits in slot $\operatorname{rev}(j)$, so the recursion computes $B_tF_t^-$ without moving whole frequency indices.

quote.quote: If $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$ reverses the $a$ binary digits of $j$, the entry $(F_t^-z)_j$ occupies slot $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$.

children.claim: The reversed level is half the inverse of the forward level, so the reverse procedure composed with $B_tF_t^-$ is $I/t$, as is $F_t^+B_t^{-1}$, and the reverse procedure computes $F_t^+B_t^{-1}$.

quote.quote: As $H_0^2=I/2$, the reversed level is half the inverse of the corresponding forward level.

children.claim: On several axes a twiddle depends only on its own axis's address bits, so a round is a parallel butterfly $\mathcal H$ followed by one recordwise monomial $J_E$, multiplication by $y^E$, and every completed round is a contraction.

quote.quote: Consequently the individual axis steps may be grouped as a parallel butterfly $\mathcal H$, followed by one recordwise monomial operation $J_E$.

children.claim: Moving each long axis's leading slot and the lowest $(\ell-1)\bmod K$ slots of every axis to a prefix costs $O(TpdK)$ and leaves each axis as consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

quote.quote: There are at most $D(b+1)=O(dK)$ listed slots, so the moves cost $O(TpdK)$.

children.claim: Reordering the remaining chunks from axis-major to chunk-index-major takes $O(p/K)$ interchanges of $K$-bit chunks, since $d\ell=O(p)$, at $O(TpK^\tau)$ each, $O(Tp\cdot pK^{\tau-1})$ in all, and these moves define $L$.

quote.quote: This uses at most $Dq-1$ exchanges of width-$K$ address chunks, even when the chunks are nonadjacent.

children.claim: In a round on the remaining chunks the selected bit has one common offset in each of the $D$ consecutive chunks of one chunk index over the complete address set, so the round is one simultaneous layer costing $O(Tpd^{\lambda'})$, $O(Tp\ell d^{\lambda'})$ over all rounds.

quote.quote: The simultaneous-layer procedure therefore applies at cost $O(Tpd^{\lambda'})$ per round and $O(Tp\ell d^{\lambda'})$ in total.

children.claim: Rounds on prefix slots apply $H_0$ to each participating bit individually, exactly on a slightly finer grid and truncated once per round, at $O(Tp)$ per participating bit and $O(TpdK)$ over at most $K$ such rounds.

quote.quote: There are at most $b+1\leq K$ rounds on prefix slots, giving cost $O(TpdK)$.

children.claim: Multiplication by $y^E$, $E=er+s$, splits the coefficient list before $r-s$, puts the negated tail first and applies the sign $(-1)^e$, in $O(rp)$ per record with no coefficient sort.

quote.quote: To implement the monomial, write $E=er+s$ with $0\leq s<r$. Split the coefficient list before position $r-s$, put its tail before its head, negate the moved tail, and apply the common sign $(-1)^e$. This is multiplication by $y^E$ modulo $y^r+1$.

children.claim: Truncation toward zero is odd and componentwise and $J_E$ is a signed coefficient permutation, so $J_EQ_p(\mathcal Hz)=Q_p(J_E\mathcal Hz)$: each round is one truncation after an exact contraction, and $\ell$ rounds give error below $\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$.

quote.quote: Thus the actual forward call sequence returns exactly the result of truncating once after the exact contraction round.

children.claim: Operating on named slots after $L$ conjugates each operation by $L$, so the forward entry with frequency address $j$ is stored at $L(Bj)$ and the opposite arithmetic consumes that order before $L^{-1}$ restores axis-major order.

quote.quote: In particular, the forward entry with frequency address $j$ is stored at $L(Bj)$.

children.claim: For disk-grid $f,g\in\mathcal R_r$ with $r=2^\ell<2^p$, the exact Gaussian integer numerators of $fg$ and then $Q_p(fg/r)$, a disk-grid polynomial within $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ of $fg/r$, are computed in $O(rp\log(rp))$ time on fixed tapes from four products of the established multiplier.
children.method: Write $f=2^{-p}(a+ib)$ and $g=2^{-p}(c+ie)$, evaluate $a,b,c,e$ at $B_0=2^{4p}$ as signed integers, form the four products with the $O(N\log N)$ multiplier, extract centered coefficients block by block, reduce modulo $y^r+1$, and truncate.

motivation.text: Evaluating at a power of two far larger than every product coefficient turns a polynomial product into one integer product whose $4p$-bit blocks determine the coefficients, so the established fast integer multiplier does all the arithmetic.

children.claim: Each evaluation $A_u=u(B_0)$ has $|A_u|<B_0^r/2$ and is formed from the coefficient stream with a carry in $\{-1,0\}$, and the four products $A_aA_c,A_bA_e,A_aA_e,A_bA_c$ come from the established multiplier.

quote.quote: Multiply the four pairs of absolute values using the established multiplier and restore each product's sign.

children.claim: Every coefficient of the ordinary products obeys $|h_j|\le r2^{2p}<2^{3p}<B_0/2$, so once the lower coefficients are removed the next one is the centered residue modulo $B_0$.

quote.quote: After the lower coefficients have been removed from an evaluation, this strict bound identifies the next coefficient by its centered residue modulo $B_0$.

children.claim: Centered extraction with a carry in $\{0,1\}$ maintains the residual identity, so every extracted block equals the true coefficient and the final carry cancels the sign extension.

quote.quote: By \eqref{eq:packing-separation}, including the padded value $h_{J-1}=0$, the unique centered representative is $h_j$ itself. Thus $\widehat h_j=h_j$.

children.claim: Reducing $ac-be$ and $ae+bc$ modulo $y^r+1$ subtracts the coefficient at $j+r$ from that at $j$, so each $H_j$ is a sum of exactly $r$ signed products, $|H_j|\le r2^{2p}$, and $\|fg/r\|_\infty\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_\infty$.

quote.quote: Thus each resulting Gaussian integer coefficient $H_j$ is a sum of exactly $r$ signed products of Gaussian integer input coefficients of modulus at most $2^p$.

children.claim: Shifting by $p+\ell$ bits gives $Q_p(fg/r)$, and the four exact integer products dominate the linear packing, extraction, wrapping and truncation costs.

quote.quote: Four exact integer products dominate the linear packing, extraction, combination, wrapping, and truncation costs.

children.claim: Since $F_{\boldsymbol t}^-(f*g)=M(F_{\boldsymbol t}^-f)(F_{\boldsymbol t}^-g)$ and $F_{\boldsymbol t}^+F_{\boldsymbol t}^-=I/M$, two forward transforms, the pointwise product $P(u,v)=uv/r$, the opposite transform and the scale $M$ give exactly $(f*g)/(rM)$, and the stored order does not interfere because $LB$ permutes whole records, so $P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v)$.

quote.quote: Since $LB$ permutes records and leaves their polynomial suffixes intact, $P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v)$.

children.claim: Two forward errors below $\sqrt2\ell\,2^{-p}$, the bilinear contraction $\|P(x,y)\|\le\|x\|\|y\|$, one product truncation and the opposite error add to less than $\sqrt2(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$ before the exact scale by $M$.

quote.quote: The final exact multiplication by $M$ therefore gives error less than $M(3\delta+\eta)=\sqrt2\,M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$, as claimed.

children.claim: The $M=T/r$ pointwise products cost $O(Tp\log(rp))$ in total, on top of the three transform costs and a linear final scaling.

quote.quote: There are $M=T/r$ pointwise polynomial products. Their total cost is $O(Tp\log(rp))$; the three transform costs are as stated, and the last exact scaling is linear in $Tp$.

children.claim: For coprime $s<t$ with $t/s-1>p/\alpha^4$ and the permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$, $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, there are contractions $A,B_0$ with $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$, computed on disk grids with error below $p^2$ in time $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$; tensoring over $d$ axes gives $RF_{\boldsymbol s}=2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A$, $\gamma=2d\alpha^2$, with error below $dp^2$, line costs $O(dTp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$ and axis movement $O(Tpd^2(1+\ell^\tau))$ in the padded box.
children.method: Use Harvey and van der Hoeven's Gaussian identity $\mathsf TP_sF_s=P_tF_t\mathsf S$ and the near-identity $N=C\mathsf T\mathsf D$, invert $N$ by a Neumann series to get a left inverse of $\mathsf T$, normalize the maps into contractions, keep $P_s$ and $P_t$ inside the identity instead of sorting, and apply the one-dimensional maps line by line, exposing axes with the chunk interchange.

motivation.text: The usual implementation sorts twice on each coordinate; keeping both permutations in the transform formula avoids executing them, since the chirp absorbs one and the other cancels in the convolution.

quote.quote: Its usual implementation sorts twice on each coordinate. We retain both permutations in the transform formula and compute that formula directly.

children.claim: With $N=C\mathsf T\mathsf D$ selecting the coordinates nearest $tj/s$, $\|N-I\|<2^{-\alpha^2\theta}<1/2$ because $\alpha^2\theta>p/\alpha^2>1$, so $N$ is invertible by the Neumann series.

quote.quote: Thus $\|N-I\|<1/2$, so $N$ is invertible by the Neumann series.

children.claim: $\mathsf DN^{-1}C$ is a left inverse of $\mathsf T$, so $\mathsf DN^{-1}CP_tF_t\mathsf S=P_sF_s$, and normalizing to $A=\mathsf S/2$ and $B_0=2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}\mathsf D\,N^{-1}C/2$ gives $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$ with contractions.

quote.quote: Applying this left inverse to the first identity in \eqref{eq:gaussian-public-facts} gives $\mathsf D N^{-1}CP_tF_t\mathsf S=P_sF_s$.

children.claim: The quoted arithmetic maps and the ordered selection $C$ give approximations of $A$ and $B_0$ with errors below $16p<p^2$ and $4+3p^2/4<p^2$.

quote.quote: Contraction of the exact maps yields errors less than $16p<p^2$ and $4+3p^2/4<p^2$, respectively.

children.claim: The original algorithm executes $P_t$ and $P_s^{-1}$ by two label-and-sort passes costing $O(tp\log t)$ each; here both permutations remain in the identity.

quote.quote: Its two label-and-sort operations implement $P_t$ and $P_s^{-1}$, each costing $O(tp\log t)$. In \eqref{eq:no-sort-one-dimensional} these permutations remain in the transform identity.

children.claim: Tensoring over all pairs $(s_i,t_i)$ gives $RF_{\boldsymbol s}=2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A$ with $R=\bigotimes_iP_{s_i}$ and $Q=\bigotimes_iP_{t_i}$.

quote.quote: Tensoring \eqref{eq:no-sort-one-dimensional} proves \eqref{eq:no-sort-tensor}.

children.claim: Applying the line maps to each valid line of the padded box and zero elsewhere keeps each axis map a contraction with error below $p^2$, so the tensor maps have error below $dp^2$ and line cost $\sum_i(T/t_i)O(t_ip^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$.

quote.quote: Composing the $d$ axis maps gives error less than $dp^2$.

children.claim: Exposing each axis takes $O(d)$ adjacent interchanges of $\ell$- or $(\ell-1)$-bit fields by the chunk interchange, peeling one bit for unequal widths, at $O(Tp(1+\ell^\tau))$ each.

quote.quote: Each adjacent interchange therefore costs $O(Tp(1+\ell^\tau))$.

children.claim: For even $t_i$ and the chirp $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp(-\pi i\sum_is_ij_i^2/t_i)$, which has period $t_i$ in coordinate $i$, the permuted middle transform is $QF_{\boldsymbol t}u=\overline a\cdot(a*(\overline a\cdot u))/T$: two pointwise phase multiplications around one normalized cyclic convolution.
children.method: Check the periodicity of $a$ and compare the coefficient of $u_{\boldsymbol k}$ on both sides, using $\overline a_{\boldsymbol j}a_{\boldsymbol j-\boldsymbol k}\overline a_{\boldsymbol k}=\exp(2\pi i\sum_is_ij_ik_i/t_i)$.

motivation.text: Bluestein's identity turns the transform into a convolution, and the coefficient $s_i$ in the chirp performs the frequency permutation $Q$, so $Q$ is never applied as a separate permutation of the array.

quote.quote: The chirp identity below performs the frequency change in $Q$ without applying $Q$ as a separate permutation of the array.

children.salient: The frequency permutation $Q$, multiplication of frequencies by $-s_i$, costs nothing: it is absorbed into the chirp's coefficients, so no sort is executed.

children.claim: Since $t_i$ is even, replacing $j_i$ by $j_i+t_i$ changes the exponent by $-\pi is_i(2j_i+t_i)\in2\pi i\mathbb Z$, so $a$ is periodic and the convolution cyclic.

quote.quote: Replacing $j_i$ by $j_i+t_i$ changes the exponent defining $a$ by $-\pi i s_i(2j_i+t_i)$, an integral multiple of $2\pi i$.

children.claim: The coefficient of $u_{\boldsymbol k}$ on the right is $T^{-1}\exp(2\pi i\sum_is_ij_ik_i/t_i)$, exactly that of $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$, since $Q$ reads frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$ of the negative-sign transform.

quote.quote: This is precisely the coefficient in $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$, because $Q$ reads frequency $(-s_i j_i)_i$ from the negative-sign transform.

children.claim: With $S=\prod_is_i$, $(RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+)[(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v)]=(u*v)/S^2$, so the retained source permutation $R$ cancels between the two forward transforms, their pointwise product and the opposite-sign transform, and conjugating input and output of an algorithm for $RF_{\boldsymbol s}$ gives one for $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+$.
children.method: Show $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=R^{-1}F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$ by substituting $h=ck$ for units $c$, commute $R$ with pointwise products, and apply the normalized convolution rule with $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+F_{\boldsymbol s}=I/S$.

motivation.text: A convolution needs the forward transforms only through their pointwise product and the opposite transform, and a dilation by units passes through the opposite transform as its inverse, so the retained permutation can cancel instead of being executed.

quote.quote: The second identity shows how the retained source permutation $R$ cancels when computing a convolution.

children.salient: The permutation $R$ is never executed: a dilation by units on the source side passes through the opposite transform as its inverse and cancels exactly.

children.claim: For a unit $c$ modulo $q$, $F_q^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F_q^+$, and each $t_i$ is a unit modulo $s_i$, so $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$.

quote.quote: Each $t_i$ is a unit modulo $s_i$, so tensoring this identity gives $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=R^{-1}F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$ and hence $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$.

children.claim: $(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v)=R(F_{\boldsymbol s}u\cdot F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$ because a coordinate permutation commutes with pointwise products.

quote.quote: Also $(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\mathbin{\cdot}(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v) =R(F_{\boldsymbol s}u\mathbin{\cdot}F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$, because a coordinate permutation commutes with pointwise products.

children.claim: With $F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=S(F_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$ and $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+F_{\boldsymbol s}=I/S$, the two normalizations give $(u*v)/S^2$.

quote.quote: The normalized convolution rule is $F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=S(F_{\boldsymbol s}u)\mathbin{\cdot} (F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$, while $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+F_{\boldsymbol s}=I/S$.

children.claim: Complex conjugation turns the negative sign into the positive one, commutes with the real permutation $R$, and preserves grid, norm and error bound.

quote.quote: Finally, conjugation changes the negative Fourier sign to the positive one and commutes with the real permutation $R$.

children.claim: With a fixed rational choice of exponents and sizes, the machine converts the inputs to radix-$2^b$ digits, maps them to prime cyclic axes, applies two computed source transforms, multiplies pointwise, applies the opposite transform, rescales, rounds and propagates carries, producing the exact $2n$-bit product within $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ steps.
children.method: Instantiate the procedures with compatible parameters, prove each reduction exact at the level of exact counterparts, track errors and disk margins through every computed map to bring the final error below $1/2$, and sum a cost table normalized by $Tp=\Theta(n)$.

motivation.text: The building blocks come with error and cost bounds under parameter hypotheses, so assembling them needs one parameter choice meeting all hypotheses, an error budget below one half for exact rounding, and a cost table whose rows are powers of $p$ below one.

adds.name: digit bit width
adds.meaning: The radix exponent: each input digit has b bits, b being the ceiling of log2 n.

adds.name: source convolution length
adds.meaning: The product of the distinct odd prime axis lengths, the length of the digit convolution.

children.claim: For all large $n$ there are distinct odd primes $s_i$ with $(1-2\eta)t_i<s_i\le(1-\eta)t_i$, $\eta=1/(4d)$, found deterministically in $n^{o(1)}$ time, so that $T/2<S<T$, each $t_i/s_i-1>\eta$ gives $\alpha^4(t_i/s_i-1)>p$, and every hypothesis of the resampling lemma holds.
children.method: Apply the prime-interval bound of Harvey and van der Hoeven (from Rosser and Schoenfeld) to the intervals below $r/2$ and $r$, each holding more than $d$ primes, multiply the lower bounds using Bernoulli's inequality, and search the intervals by trial division.

motivation.text: The product of the source lengths must fill a fixed fraction of the padded box, while each ratio $t_i/s_i$ must stay separated from one for resampling, so the primes must lie just below the powers of two but not too close.

quote.quote: The distinct prime lengths $s_i$ must be close to the powers of two $t_i$: their product must occupy a fixed fraction of the padded box, while each ratio $t_i/s_i$ must leave enough separation for resampling.

children.claim: Since $\log(r/2)/d\to\infty$, both $x=r/2$ and $x=r$ satisfy $\log x>8d=2/\eta$, so each interval $((1-2\eta)x,(1-\eta)x]$ holds at least $x/(8d\log x)>d$ primes, and the two intervals are disjoint.

quote.quote: Thus both $x=r/2$ and $x=r$ satisfy $\log x>8d=2/\eta$.

children.claim: Multiplying the lower bounds and using Bernoulli's inequality gives $S/T>(1-1/(2d))^d>1/2$, so $T/2<S<T$.

quote.quote: Together with $s_i<t_i$, this gives $T/2<S<T$.

children.claim: Each $t_i/s_i-1\ge\eta/(1-\eta)>\eta$ gives $\alpha^4(t_i/s_i-1)>12d^2b/(4d)=3db\ge p$, and with $2\le\alpha<\sqrt p$ and $t_i<2^p$ every hypothesis of the resampling lemma holds.

quote.quote: Thus every hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:no-sort-resampling} holds for all sufficiently large input lengths.

children.claim: Trial-division search costs $O(dr^{3/2}\operatorname{poly}(p))$, whose logarithm is $o(p)$, hence $n^{o(1)}$ time, and the primes are computed by the machine rather than supplied as advice.
